readings.title: The Law of Vows
readings.subtitle: Binding Oaths and the Authority of Fathers and Husbands
readings.text: [Numbers 30:1] And Mosheh spoke to the heads of the tribes concerning the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, “This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded: [2] “When a man vows a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, or swears an oath to bind himself by some agreement, he does not break his word, he does according to all that comes out of his mouth. [3] “Or if a woman vows a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and binds herself by some agreement while in her father’s house in her youth, [4] and her father hears <dn>את</dn> her vow and the agreement by which she has bound herself, and her father has kept silent towards her, then all her vows shall stand, and every agreement with which she has bound herself stands. [5] “But if her father forbids <dn>את</dn> her on the day that he hears, then none of her vows nor her agreements by which she has bound herself stand. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pardons her, because her father has forbidden <dn>את</dn> her. [6] “But if she at all belongs to a husband, while bound by her vows or by a rash utterance from her lips by which she bound herself, [7] and her husband hears it, and he has kept silent towards her on the day that he hears, then her vows shall stand, and her agreements by which she bound herself do stand. [8] “But if her husband forbids <dn>את</dn> her on the day that he hears it, then he has nullified <dn>את</dn> her vow which she vowed, and <dn>את</dn> the rash utterance of her lips by which she bound herself, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pardons her. [9] “But any vow of a widow or a divorced woman, by which she has bound herself, stands against her. [10] “And if she vowed in her husband’s house, or bound herself by an agreement with an oath, [11] and her husband heard it, and has kept silent towards her and did not forbid <dn>את</dn> her, then all her vows shall stand, and every agreement by which she bound herself stands. [12] “But if her husband clearly nullified <dn>את</dn> them on the day he heard them, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows or concerning the agreement binding her, it does not stand – her husband has nullified them, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pardons her. [13] “Every vow and every binding oath to afflict her being, let her husband confirm it, or let her husband nullify it. [14] “But if her husband is altogether silent at her from day to day, then he confirms <dn>את</dn> all her vows or <dn>את</dn> all the agreements that bind her – he confirms <dn>את</dn> them, because he kept silent towards her on the day that he heard. [15] “But if he nullifies <dn>את</dn> them after he has heard, then he shall bear <dn>את</dn> her crookedness.” [16] These are the laws which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh, between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.

readings.title: Vengeance on Midian
readings.subtitle: The Defeat of the Midianites and Purification of the Spoil
readings.text: [Numbers 31:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Take vengeance for the children of Yisra’ěl on <dn>את</dn> the Miḏyanites. After that you are to be gathered to your people.”</dq> [3] And Mosheh spoke to the people, saying, “Arm some of yourselves for the campaign, and let them go against the Miḏyanites to take vengeance for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on Miḏyan. [4] “Send a thousand from each tribe of all the tribes of Yisra’ěl for the campaign.” [5] So there were supplied from the tribes of Yisra’ěl one thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand armed ones for the campaign. [6] And Mosheh sent <dn>את</dn> them on the campaign, one thousand from each tribe, <dn>את</dn> them and <dn>את</dn> Pineḥas son of El‛azar the priest on the campaign, with the set-apart utensils and the trumpets for sounding in his hand. [7] And they fought against the Miḏyanites, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh, and killed all the males. [8] And they killed <dn>את</dn> the sovereigns of Miḏyan with the rest of those who were pierced: <dn>את</dn> Evi, and <dn>את</dn> Reqem, and <dn>את</dn> Tsur, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥur, and <dn>את</dn> Reḇa, the five sovereigns of Miḏyan. And they killed <dn>את</dn> Bil‛am son of Be‛or with the sword. [9] And the sons of Yisra’ěl took <dn>את</dn> the women of Miḏyan captive, with <dn>את</dn> their little ones, and took as spoil <dn>את</dn> all their livestock, and <dn>את</dn> all their possessions. [10] And they burned with fire <dn>את</dn> all the cities where they dwelt, and <dn>את</dn> all their settlements. [11] And they took <dn>את</dn> all the spoil and <dn>את</dn> all the booty, both of man and beast. [12] And they brought <dn>את</dn> the captives, and <dn>את</dn> the booty, and <dn>את</dn> the spoil to Mosheh, and to El‛azar the priest, and to the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl, to the camp in the desert plains of Mo’aḇ by the Yarděn of Yeriḥo. [13] And Mosheh, and El‛azar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation, went to meet them outside the camp. [14] But Mosheh was wroth with the officers of the army, with the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, who had come from the campaign. [15] And Mosheh said to them, “Have you kept all the women alive? [16] “Look, they are the ones who caused the children of Yisra’ěl, through the word of Bil‛am, to trespass against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the matter of Pe‛or, and there was a plague among the congregation of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] “And now, kill every male among the little ones. And every woman who has known a man by lying with a man you shall kill. [18] “But keep alive for yourselves all the female children who have not known a man by lying with a man. [19] “And you, camp outside the camp seven days. Whoever has killed any being, and whoever has touched any slain, cleanse yourselves and your captives on the third day and on the seventh day. [20] “And cleanse every garment, and every object of leather and all the work of goats’ hair, and every object of wood.” [21] And El‛azar the priest said to the men of the campaign who went to the battle, “This is the law of the Torah which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh: [22] “Only <dn>את</dn> the gold, and <dn>את</dn> the silver, <dn>את</dn> the bronze, <dn>את</dn> the iron, <dn>את</dn> the tin, and <dn>את</dn> the lead, [23] every object that passes through fire, you put through the fire, and it shall be clean; only, let it be cleansed with the water for uncleanness. And whatever does not pass through fire you pass through water. [24] “And you shall wash your garments on the seventh day and be clean, and afterwards come into the camp.”

readings.title: Division of the Plunder
readings.subtitle: The Spoils of War and the Offering to YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Numbers 31:25] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [26] <dq>“Count up <dn>את</dn> the plunder that was taken, of man and of beast, you and El‛azar the priest and the heads of the fathers of the congregation.</dq> [27] <dq>“And you shall divide <dn>את</dn> the plunder into two parts, between those who took part in the battle, who went out on the campaign, and all the congregation.</dq> [28] <dq>“And set aside a levy for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on <dn>את</dn> the men of battle who went out on the campaign: one out of every five hundred, of man, and of the cattle, and of the donkeys, and of the sheep.</dq> [29] <dq>“Take it from their half, and give it to El‛azar the priest as a contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [30] <dq>“And from the children of Yisra’ěl’s half you shall take one of every fifty, of man, of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the sheep, of all the livestock, and give <dn>את</dn> them to the Lěvites guarding the duty of the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> [31] And Mosheh and El‛azar the priest did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [32] And the booty remaining from the plunder, which the people of the campaign had taken, was six hundred and seventy-five thousand sheep, [33] and seventy-two thousand cattle, [34] and sixty-one thousand donkeys, [35] and thirty-two thousand human beings in all, of women who had not known a man by lying with a man. [36] And the half, the portion for those who went out on the campaign, was in number three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep, [37] and the levy unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of the sheep was six hundred and seventy-five. [38] And the cattle were thirty-six thousand, of which the levy unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was seventy-two. [39] And the donkeys were thirty thousand five hundred, of which the levy unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was sixty-one. [40] And the human beings were sixteen thousand, of which the levy unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was thirty-two beings. [41] So Mosheh gave <dn>את</dn> the levy which was the contribution unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to El‛azar the priest, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [42] And from the children of Yisra’ěl’s half, which Mosheh divided from the men who campaigned: [43] now the half belonging to the congregation was three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep, [44] and thirty-six thousand cattle, [45] and thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, [46] and sixteen thousand human beings. [47] Then Mosheh took from the children of Yisra’ěl’s half: <dn>את</dn> one out of every fifty, drawn from man and beast, and gave <dn>את</dn> them to the Lěvites, who guarded the duty of the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. [48] And the officers who were over thousands of the campaign, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, came near to Mosheh, [49] and they said to Mosheh, “Your servants have taken <dn>את</dn> a count of the fighting men under our command, and not a man of us is missing. [50] “So we have brought <dn>את</dn> an offering for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, what every man found of ornaments of gold: armlets and bracelets and signet rings and earrings and necklaces, to make atonement for ourselves before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [51] And Mosheh and El‛azar the priest received <dn>את</dn> the gold from <dn>את</dn> them, all the fashioned ornaments. [52] And all the gold of the offering that they presented to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, from <dn>את</dn> the commanders of thousands and <dn>את</dn> commanders of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty sheqels. [53] The men of the campaign had taken spoil, every man for himself. [54] And Mosheh and El‛azar the priest received <dn>את</dn> the gold from <dn>את</dn> the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and brought <dn>את</dn> it into the Tent of Appointment as a remembrance for the children of Yisra’ěl before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
